papers.title: A systems biology network analysis of root resorption biomarkers and their clinical relevance in orthodontics: a pilot study.
papers.abstract: External apical root resorption is a frequently reported iatrogenic consequence of orthodontic tooth movement. This pilot study used an integrated systems biology approach to identify signaling pathways, key genes, and candidate salivary biomarkers associated with orthodontic root resorption to support future functional research.
papers.summary: This pilot study applies systems biology network analysis to identify signaling pathways, hub genes, and candidate salivary biomarkers associated with external apical root resorption during orthodontic tooth movement. The work is exploratory and aims to prioritize targets for future functional validation rather than provide definitive clinical biomarkers.

papers.title: Endothelial SLC25A13 links glutamine metabolism to angiogenesis.
papers.abstract: Attention to exploring endothelial cell (EC) metabolism is increasing, but a holistic perspective on the metabolic adaptations of ECs during angiogenic proliferation is still missing. Here, we use a previously in-house developed computational EC-adapted genome-scale metabolic model that recapitulates known metabolic features in proliferating ECs to predict novel pathways central to biomass synthesis. We unveil the metabolic function of the glutamate-aspartate antiporter SLC25A13, previously overlooked in ECs, as a key regulator of glutamine utilization and provide evidence regarding its contri
papers.summary: Using an endothelial cell-adapted genome-scale metabolic model, the authors predicted and validated that the mitochondrial glutamate-aspartate antiporter SLC25A13 is a key regulator of glutamine utilization in proliferating endothelial cells. This previously overlooked transporter supports biomass synthesis and angiogenesis, linking glutamine metabolism to new blood vessel formation.

papers.title: Enhancing 3-hydroxypropionic acid production in Komagataella phaffii via methanol and formate co-feeding.
papers.abstract: Komagataella phaffii is a promising cell factory that can use CO2 derived methanol, a sustainable carbon (C1) source, for chemical production. Introducing the ß-alanine biosynthetic pathway alongside a NADP+-dependent formate dehydrogenase (FDH) in K. phaffii enables the production of the platform chemical 3-hydroxypropionic acid (3-HP). Co-feeding of formate and methanol (MeOH) was systematically explored to enhance cellular reducing power and improve 3-HP biosynthesis. Implementing a pulsed formate strategy alongside MeOH resulted in up to a 20.7% increase in 3-HP per gram of MeOH (Yg3-HP gM
papers.summary: This study engineers the yeast Komagataella phaffii to produce 3-hydroxypropionic acid (3-HP), a platform chemical, from methanol by introducing a β-alanine pathway and a NADP+-dependent formate dehydrogenase. Co-feeding formate with methanol in a pulsed strategy boosts cellular reducing power and increases 3-HP yield per gram of methanol by up to 20.7%. The work demonstrates a C1-based biomanufacturing approach for a valuable chemical.

papers.title: Harnessing computational intelligence for synthetic lethality: A roadmap from network biology to interpretable deep learning in precision oncology.
papers.abstract: Synthetic lethality (SL) is an emerging therapeutic paradigm in precision oncology that enables the selective targeting of cancer cells based on their specific genetic vulnerabilities. Despite its clinical promise, the enormous combinatorial search space of gene-gene interactions poses a major challenge for experimental screening. This review provides a critical survey of computational SL discovery, moving beyond sequential descriptions to offer a comparative synthesis of architectures ranging from traditional network-based models to advanced graph transformers and knowledge graph reasoning. W
papers.summary: This review surveys computational approaches for discovering synthetic lethal gene pairs in cancer, comparing traditional network-based models with newer graph transformer and knowledge graph reasoning methods. It argues that interpretable deep learning architectures can help navigate the vast combinatorial search space of gene-gene interactions more efficiently than experimental screening alone.

papers.title: Let there be multifunctionality: Uncovering the dynamical zoo of the AC-DC genetic circuit.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) govern many cell processes. While multistability and oscillations are common GRN dynamics, they are typically studied and engineered in isolation. Here, we challenge this separation using the AC-DC circuit, a minimal three-gene network that merges the classical toggle switch and repressilator. Using a thermodynamic formalism and Bayesian inference, we show that a single-inducer version of the circuit displays diverse multifunctional dynamics, including coexistence of oscillations and multistability. We explore robustness, classify emergent behaviors, and analyze
papers.summary: This study analyzes the AC-DC genetic circuit, a three-gene network combining a toggle switch and a repressilator, and shows that a single-inducer version can exhibit multiple dynamical behaviors simultaneously, including coexisting oscillations and multistability. Using thermodynamic modeling and Bayesian inference, the authors map out a 'dynamical zoo' of behaviors and assess their robustness, challenging the traditional separation of these dynamics in synthetic biology.

papers.title: Robust identification of cell-cell communication heterogeneity in single cells.
papers.abstract: Cell-cell communication modulates cell fate decisions by relaying information across tissues and inducing intracellular responses mediated by gene regulatory networks. Although the inference of cell-cell communication from high-throughput data is gaining popularity, studying how communication pathways operate across biological scales and influence cell fate decisions remains challenging. Here, we present scRICH (robust identification of cell-cell communication heterogeneity in single cells), a computational framework that leverages single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data to unravel the he
papers.summary: The authors present scRICH, a computational framework that infers cell-cell communication from single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data while accounting for heterogeneity across cells. It aims to reveal how communication pathways operate across biological scales and influence cell fate decisions. This provides a more robust way to study intercellular signaling than existing inference methods.

papers.title: Revisiting Ehrlich carcinoma in the era of precision oncology: bridging classical models with modern systems biology.
papers.abstract: Ehrlich carcinoma (EC) and its ascitic form, Ehrlich ascites carcinoma (EAC), are among the oldest and most widely used experimental tumor models in cancer research. Although they have traditionally been used for anticancer drug screening, their potential to address broader aspects of aggressive tumor biology has received comparatively less attention. EC/EAC exhibits several characteristics associated with advanced malignancy, including rapid tumor growth, angiogenesis, immune dysregulation, metabolic changes, therapeutic resistance, and complex interactions between the tumor and host. These f
papers.summary: This review argues that Ehrlich carcinoma and Ehrlich ascites carcinoma, despite being among the oldest experimental tumor models, remain underused for studying aggressive tumor biology beyond simple drug screening. The authors highlight how EC/EAC captures features of advanced malignancy—rapid growth, angiogenesis, immune dysregulation, metabolic reprogramming, therapeutic resistance, and tumor-host interactions—and propose integrating these classical models with modern systems biology and precision oncology approaches.

papers.title: Host-like temperature unlocks glucose uptake and metabolism in pathogenic Leptospira.
papers.abstract: Pathogenic Leptospira transitions between environmental reservoirs and mammalian hosts, exposing the bacterium to distinct temperature conditions. Although Leptospira is generally considered to rely primarily on long-chain fatty acids for growth and to have limited capacity to use glucose, whether host-like temperature alters glucose-associated metabolic capacity remains unclear. Here, we used transcriptome-integrated genome-scale metabolic modeling to examine temperature-dependent metabolic states in pathogenic Leptospira. Models contextualized with transcriptomic data from cultures at 37°C p
papers.summary: Using transcriptome-integrated genome-scale metabolic modeling, the authors show that host-like temperature (37°C) enables pathogenic Leptospira to take up and metabolize glucose, contrary to the long-held view that this pathogen relies mainly on long-chain fatty acids. This temperature-dependent metabolic shift may be important for survival and virulence within mammalian hosts.

papers.title: Uncovering combination therapies for immune-mediated inflammatory diseases through systems biology analysis on longitudinal patient data.
papers.abstract: While targeted therapies have reshaped the clinical management of immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs), primary non-response remains a major obstacle for many patients. Combining two targeted therapies is an emerging strategy to overcome this therapeutic ceiling, but the number of possible drug pairs makes prioritization difficult. For this objective, we present mitigation of non-response signature (MNRS), a computational approach that uses longitudinal blood transcriptomic data from six IMIDs treated with different targeted therapies to identify the most promising drug combinations.
papers.summary: The authors present MNRS, a computational method that uses longitudinal blood transcriptomic data from patients with six immune-mediated inflammatory diseases to prioritize combination therapies that could overcome primary non-response to targeted drugs. By identifying drug pairs that mitigate non-response signatures, the approach narrows the large space of possible combinations to the most promising candidates. This offers a systems-biology framework for rational combination therapy design in IMIDs.

papers.title: Modeling microbiome modulation of tumor metabolic networks to predict synergistic therapies.
papers.abstract: Differences in microbiome composition profoundly influence drug response, yet methods to model the metabolic impact of microbes on host cells and therapeutics remain limited. We present a microbiome-aware computational framework combining machine learning and genome-scale metabolic models to predict combination therapies for colorectal cancer (CRC) in the presence of Fusobacterium nucleatum (Fn) and other pathogenic, probiotic, and commensal microbes. The model learned predictive metabolic flux signatures from 6,514 drug combination profiles in CRC cell lines and predicted synergistic drug com
papers.summary: The authors developed a computational framework that integrates machine learning with genome-scale metabolic models to predict how gut microbes, particularly Fusobacterium nucleatum, alter tumor metabolic networks and drug responses in colorectal cancer. Trained on 6,514 drug combination profiles, the model identifies metabolic flux signatures that predict synergistic combination therapies in the presence of different microbial communities. This provides a new approach for microbiome-aware drug combination design.

papers.title: Metabolic modeling with reverse mapping links host perturbations to Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
papers.abstract: Understanding host-pathogen interactions during Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infection has largely relied on identifying bacterial genes essential for intracellular survival. However, conventional reverse genetics approaches often overlook host pathways that regulate Mtb growth. Here, we developed a backtracing strategy to link host metabolic modulators with specific Mtb proteins. A genome-scale host metabolic model integrated with lung transcriptomic data from H37Rv-infected mice predicted 18 host proteins essential for Mtb survival. We validated this through pharmacological inhibition, s
papers.summary: The authors developed a computational 'backtracing' strategy that integrates a genome-scale host metabolic model with lung transcriptomic data from Mtb-infected mice to identify host proteins whose metabolic activity supports bacterial survival. They predicted 18 host proteins essential for Mtb growth and validated these through pharmacological inhibition. This approach complements traditional bacterial reverse genetics by revealing host metabolic vulnerabilities that could be targeted therapeutically.

papers.title: Integrative analysis of Alzheimer's disease molecular networks with circadian regulators for prioritization of drug repurposing candidates.
papers.abstract: BackgroundAlzheimer's disease (AD) is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder characterized by complex molecular mechanisms. Growing evidence indicates that circadian rhythm disruption contributes to disease progression and interacts with pathogenic pathways. Although multi-omics resources, compound perturbation profiles, and pharmacological bioactivity data are increasingly available, their integrative use for drug repurposing prioritization in AD, particularly with explicit consideration of circadian rhythm, remains limited.ObjectiveThis study aimed to prioritize drug repurposing candida
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics Alzheimer's disease network data with circadian rhythm regulators and compound perturbation/pharmacological bioactivity data to prioritize drug repurposing candidates. By explicitly incorporating circadian biology into network-based analysis, it identifies candidate drugs that may act on AD-relevant pathways linked to circadian disruption. The work offers a computational framework for hypothesis generation rather than experimental validation.

papers.title: Gene Regulatory Network Reconstruction to Decipher the Molecular Mechanisms Governing Bacteriocyte-Based Symbioses.
papers.abstract: Intracellular bacteria with beneficial roles for their hosts are present in more than 10% of all insect species. In intracellular nutritional symbioses, these symbionts are typically confined to specialized host cells known as bacteriocytes. Bacteriocytes are remarkable novel cells that arose independently and repeatedly across multiple insect lineages. They are fascinating structures, yet the molecular mechanisms regulating their development, function and even their evolutionary origins, remain largely unknown. Nonetheless, an important role for certain transcription factors in development an
papers.summary: This review discusses how reconstructing gene regulatory networks can reveal the molecular mechanisms controlling bacteriocyte development and function in insect-bacteria nutritional symbioses. Bacteriocytes are specialized host cells that house beneficial intracellular bacteria and evolved independently across many insect lineages, yet the regulatory programs governing their development and evolutionary origins remain poorly understood. The authors highlight the role of specific transcription factors and argue that network reconstruction approaches can help decipher these mechanisms.

papers.title: Whole-cell spatiotemporal model and multimodal data illuminate the multiscale light responses in a photosynthetic bacterium.
papers.abstract: Photosynthetic microorganisms rely on multiple central carbon metabolism pathways to adapt to fluctuating light and energy availability across diel cycles. Mechanistic insight into the regulatory dynamics of this adaptation requires integrating processes that operate across disparate timescales, from rapid redox-dependent post-translational modifications (PTMs) to slower changes in protein expression and metabolic pathway usage. Here, we develop a whole-cell 4D (3D + time) model of the marine cyanobacterium Prochlorococcus marinus MED4 that explicitly represents the spatial, subcellular organi
papers.summary: The authors built a whole-cell 4D (space + time) computational model of the marine cyanobacterium Prochlorococcus marinus MED4, integrating spatial organization, redox-dependent post-translational modifications, protein expression changes, and central carbon metabolism. Combined with multimodal data, the model reveals how processes across timescales—from rapid PTMs to slower expression shifts—coordinate multiscale light responses in this photosynthetic bacterium.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence for Plant Gene Regulatory Networks.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) are the maps that plant biologists most want to draw, with arrows pointing from transcription factors to the genes they control, explaining how plants develop and respond to the environment. Since experimental validation of even one arrow can take years, and a single plant genome harbours tens of millions of candidate TF-target pairs, this gap has driven the development of numerous computational methods for GRN inference. Here I review three generations of computational approaches to plant GRN inference and measure them against a five-level ladder of evidence, i
papers.summary: This review traces three generations of computational methods for inferring plant gene regulatory networks, from early co-expression approaches to modern machine-learning models. It evaluates these methods against a five-level ladder of evidence, highlighting the gap between computational predictions and experimentally validated regulatory interactions. The review argues that AI-driven approaches are essential given the millions of candidate transcription factor-target pairs in plant genomes.

papers.title: Rhizobia bacteroid transcription helps to coordinate the soybean nodule drought response.
papers.abstract: Soybean (Glycine max L. [Merr.]) nitrogen fixation is sensitive to soil drying and is an important target for improving soybean drought resilience. Transcriptional regulation of the nodule drought response and the influence of symbiotic rhizobia are not well understood. We measured whole-plant responses to mild and moderate soil moisture deficit (41% and 20% of field capacity) alongside the nodule transcriptome, including soybean and Bradyrhizobium diazoefficiens transcripts, in two soybean genotypes ('Benning' and PI 471938) that were previously found to have diverging nitrogen fixation droug
papers.summary: This study examined how soybean nodules respond to mild and moderate drought at the whole-plant and transcriptome level, including both soybean and its symbiotic rhizobia (Bradyrhizobium diazoefficiens) transcripts, in two genotypes with differing nitrogen fixation drought tolerance. The findings suggest that rhizobia bacteroid transcription actively contributes to coordinating the nodule drought response, not just the plant host. This highlights the symbiont's transcriptional role in modulating nitrogen fixation under water deficit.

papers.title: CardamomOT: A mechanistic optimal transport-based framework for gene regulatory network inference, trajectory reconstruction and generative modeling.
papers.abstract: A key challenge in inferring gene regulatory networks (GRNs) governing cellular processes such as differentiation and reprogramming from experimental data lies in the impossibility of directly measuring protein dynamics at the single-cell level, which prevents establishing causal relationships between regulator activity and target responses. In earlier work, we introduced CARDAMOM, an algorithm that uses temporal snapshots of scRNA-seq data to calibrate a GRN-driven mechanistic model of gene expression. However, this method had several limitations: it could only rely on the relative ordering o
papers.summary: CardamomOT extends the CARDAMOM algorithm for inferring gene regulatory networks from single-cell RNA-seq time courses by incorporating optimal transport, which allows the method to use actual time-point information rather than just the relative ordering of snapshots. The framework simultaneously reconstructs differentiation trajectories and supports generative modeling of cellular dynamics. This addresses a key limitation of the original method, enabling more accurate causal inference of regulator-target relationships from snapshot data.

papers.title: Thermo-flux: generation and analysis of thermodynamic-stoichiometric metabolic network models.
papers.abstract: Metabolic modeling with stoichiometric models and flux balance analysis (FBA) has greatly advanced our understanding of metabolism. However, valid FBA predictions require mechanistically correct constraints. Thermodynamic constraints can increase the mechanistic foundations of stoichiometric models and reduce the solution space, but incorporating them has so far required cumbersome manual effort. To circumvent manual curation, we introduce 'Thermo-Flux', a semi-automated Python package that converts stoichiometric models into comprehensive thermodynamic-stoichiometric models. 'Thermo-Flux' ena
papers.summary: Thermo-Flux is a semi-automated Python package that converts existing stoichiometric metabolic models into thermodynamic-stoichiometric models by integrating thermodynamic constraints, reducing the need for manual curation. This allows flux balance analysis predictions to be more mechanistically grounded and narrows the solution space, improving model accuracy.

papers.title: From plasmid sequence to process design: A computational analysis of metabolism in the context of plasmid DNA manufacturing.
papers.abstract: Detailed understanding of plasmid-host physiological interactions and recombinant protein expression is crucial for the design and optimization of plasmid DNA (pDNA) manufacturing processes. Successfully transformed host cells carrying one or more copies of a particular plasmid exhibit modified metabolic behavior which may include reduced specific growth rate, increased metabolic resource cycling (ATP/ADP, NAD/NADH, NADP/NADPH) and, in some cases, even modified nutrient uptake and metabolite secretion rates. Mapping plasmid design features to critical process parameters (CPPs), such as specifi
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational framework that links plasmid sequence features to host-cell metabolic behavior in order to inform the design and optimization of plasmid DNA manufacturing processes. It models how transformed cells with plasmid copies show altered growth, energy cofactor cycling, and nutrient uptake/secretion, and maps plasmid design features onto critical process parameters. The work aims to support rational process design by connecting sequence-level information to measurable bioprocess outcomes.

papers.title: Systems biology-driven drug repurposing in glioblastoma via antigen and pathway mapping.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive brain tumor with limited treatment options and poor patient survival. This study aimed to identify key genes and altered pathways in GBM and to explore potential drug-repurposing candidates using a systems biology approach.
papers.summary: This study applies a systems biology workflow to glioblastoma, integrating gene expression and pathway data to identify key dysregulated genes and pathways, then maps these to candidate drugs for repurposing. The output is a set of antigen and pathway targets with corresponding repurposing hypotheses, rather than experimental validation.

papers.title: Biological limits of lifespan extension: Evidence for a shift from pathway leverage to system-level buffering across species.
papers.abstract: Interventions targeting conserved aging pathways can markedly extend lifespan in model organisms, yet their efficacy declines with increasing organismal complexity. While this phenomenon is well documented, the underlying constraints remain poorly defined. Here, we integrate comparative experimental data with mechanistic insights to propose a unifying framework explaining the declining ceiling of lifespan extension. We show that in simple organisms, aging is governed by a limited number of high-leverage pathways, whereas in mammals it emerges from distributed, multi-tissue regulatory systems c
papers.summary: This review proposes a conceptual framework explaining why interventions targeting conserved aging pathways extend lifespan robustly in simple organisms but have diminishing effects in mammals. The authors argue that aging shifts from being controlled by a few high-leverage pathways in simple organisms to distributed, multi-tissue regulatory systems in complex ones, so that system-level buffering limits the ceiling of lifespan extension.

papers.title: Cell dynamics on energy landscape: Comparing attractor detection in Boolean network and diffusion-based models under in silico gene perturbations.
papers.abstract: Steady-state attractor detection differs fundamentally between discrete Boolean network (BN) and continuous diffusion-based models because they operate on different state spaces and exhibit distinct dynamic behaviors. Here, we propose cell dynamics on energy landscape (CellLand) to systematically compare BN and diffusion-based approaches for quantifying cellular dynamics on the energy landscape, with a particular focus on attractor identification under in silico gene perturbations. Although the energy landscape provides a unifying conceptual framework, BN-based models face specific challenges,
papers.summary: This paper introduces CellLand, a framework for comparing how discrete Boolean network models and continuous diffusion-based models identify steady-state attractors on an energy landscape, especially under simulated gene perturbations. It highlights that while the energy landscape offers a unifying conceptual view, Boolean network approaches face specific challenges in this context. The work provides a systematic comparison to guide model choice for studying cellular dynamics.

papers.title: Population-specific transcriptomic shifts underlie secondary metabolic diversification in Aspergillus flavus Link and the domestication of Aspergillus oryzae (Ahlb.).
papers.abstract: The genomic signatures of microbial domestication remain poorly understood within the context of natural population variation. Here, we demonstrate that Aspergillus oryzae, the filamentous fungus used in soy sauce and sake production, shares more recent ancestry with a predominantly northern, largely non-aflatoxigenic population of Aspergillus flavus (population C). A. oryzae isolates also overlap with the recently described, clinically enriched A. flavus population D, suggesting multiple domestication events. All isolates tested retained pathogenicity in a zebrafish infection model. At the tr
papers.summary: This study shows that the domesticated fungus Aspergillus oryzae, used in soy sauce and sake production, is most closely related to a northern, largely non-aflatoxigenic population (population C) of the wild species A. flavus, with additional overlap to a clinically enriched population D, pointing to multiple domestication events. Transcriptomic comparisons reveal population-specific shifts in secondary metabolism, and all tested isolates retained pathogenicity in a zebrafish infection model. The work links natural population variation to domestication signatures in a filamentous fungus.

papers.title: Immunogenic cell death and tertiary lymphoid structures jointly define dysregulated antitumor immune states and therapeutic vulnerability in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Immunogenic cell death (ICD) and tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) are biologically distinct yet interconnected components of antitumor immunity. ICD promotes danger-associated immune activation, whereas TLSs organize local adaptive immune responses. However, how these processes jointly affect immune heterogeneity, prognosis, and therapeutic responsiveness in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study examines how immunogenic cell death (ICD) and tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) jointly shape antitumor immunity in lung adenocarcinoma. By integrating these two biologically distinct but interconnected immune processes, the authors identify dysregulated immune states that link to prognosis and therapeutic vulnerability, suggesting combined ICD/TLS profiling could help stratify patients for immunotherapy.

papers.title: GP-DHT: A dual-head transformer with supervised contrastive learning for shared-gene pretraining and single-cell GRN prediction.
papers.abstract: Gene Regulatory Networks (GRNs) are crucial for understanding cell fate decisions and disease mechanisms. However, inferring GRNs from single-cell RNA sequencing remains challenging due to noise, data sparsity, and species-specific distribution variations. We propose GP-DHT (Gene Pair-Dual Head Transformer), a single-cell GRN inference framework that pre-trains gene representations on a unified shared gene space using the BEELINE datasets of humans and mice. It models gene-cell expression relationships through a multi-relational heterograph and predicts transcription factor (TF)-target regulat
papers.summary: GP-DHT is a dual-head transformer framework that pre-trains gene representations on a unified shared-gene space across human and mouse BEELINE datasets and then predicts transcription factor–target regulatory links from single-cell RNA-seq. It models gene–cell expression relationships via a multi-relational heterograph and uses supervised contrastive learning to improve GRN inference under noise, sparsity, and cross-species distribution shifts.

papers.title: Towards epigenetically informed and biobank-driven precision immunotherapy in melanoma.
papers.abstract: Cutaneous melanoma (CM) is a highly immunogenic and therapeutically intricate solid tumor, exemplifying the interactions between tumors and the immune system. Despite the significant enhancement in survival rates for patients with advanced melanoma due to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), numerous patients either exhibit resistance to these agents or develop immune evasion mechanisms. This underscores the pressing necessity to identify biological determinants of drug responses. A significant body of research indicates that epigenetic alterations, including DNA methylation, histone modificat
papers.summary: This review discusses how epigenetic changes such as DNA methylation and histone modifications influence melanoma's response to immune checkpoint inhibitors, and argues that integrating epigenetic data with large biobank resources could enable more precise immunotherapy. It highlights the need to identify biological determinants of drug resistance and immune evasion to guide patient selection.

papers.title: Host-directed therapeutics against antimicrobial-resistant bacterial infections: emerging roles of multi-omics and systems biology.
papers.abstract: The rapid emergence and global dissemination of antimicrobial resistance (AMR), coupled with the limited development of new antimicrobial agents, have intensified concerns regarding a major global public health crisis. Although antibiotic resistance is primarily driven by microbial mechanisms, host immune and inflammatory responses also play critical roles in determining infection outcomes, pathogen persistence, and treatment efficacy. In this context, host-directed therapies (HDTs) have emerged as a promising complementary strategy by modulating host pathways to enhance antimicrobial immunity
papers.summary: This review discusses how host-directed therapies (HDTs) can complement antibiotics against antimicrobial-resistant infections by modulating host immune and inflammatory pathways rather than targeting the pathogen directly. It highlights emerging roles for multi-omics and systems biology approaches in identifying host targets and understanding infection outcomes, offering a framework for developing new therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Neuro-psycho MMSig: multimodal mechanism enrichment platform for neuropsychiatric disorders.
papers.abstract: Understanding the pathophysiology of neurodegenerative and psychiatric disorders requires integrating multimodal data.
papers.summary: The authors present Neuro-psycho MMSig, a platform that integrates multimodal data to identify enriched biological mechanisms underlying neurodegenerative and psychiatric disorders. The tool aims to help researchers connect genetic, transcriptomic, and other data types to disease pathophysiology. This is a methods/tool contribution with potential utility for neuropsychiatric research.

papers.title: Probiogenomics as a Computational Biotechnology Framework: Safety-Gated Genome Analytics for Candidate Probiotic Prioritization and Validation.
papers.abstract: Whole-genome sequencing has transformed probiotic discovery into a strain-resolved computational problem, but genome data alone cannot establish probiotic efficacy, complete safety, or regulatory acceptability. This review frames probiogenomics as a safety-gated decision-support framework for candidate probiotic prioritization and validation. The framework integrates strain provenance, genome quality, strain authentication, taxonomic confidence, antimicrobial resistance screening, virulence and toxin assessment, plasmid, prophage and mobile-element analysis, undesirable metabolite screening, f
papers.summary: This review proposes probiogenomics as a computational decision-support framework for prioritizing and validating probiotic candidates, emphasizing that genome data alone cannot establish efficacy or safety. The framework integrates strain provenance, genome quality, taxonomic confidence, antimicrobial resistance screening, virulence and toxin assessment, mobile-element analysis, and metabolite screening into a safety-gated workflow.
